title: PRIMAL FX: two supplement orders, two packaging formats
description: Two PRIMAL FX order examples show how product shape and order contents guide carton and letterbox packaging, with barcode, batch and expiry handling.
summary: Two PRIMAL FX order examples show how product shape and order contents guide carton and letterbox packaging, with barcode, batch and expiry handling.

sections.heading: A practical look at supplement fulfilment
paragraphs: A three-product order and a single-pouch order call for different packaging. These two PRIMAL FX examples, supplied by Vareya on 10 November 2026, show how the order contents inform picking, packing and shipping selection. The dimensions, weights and processing times below are the figures reported for these examples, rather than a promise for every order.

sections.heading: Spain: three-product carton order (labelled NonBoxable)
paragraphs: Order #503086 contained one FENUGREEK (FPF-0059-120), one MAGNESIUM + Lysine M6 (FPF-0002-60) and one LIVER (FPF-0043-180). Vareya reports a branded carton measuring 213 × 153 × 109 mm and a shipment weight of 500 g. Protective material and a thank-you card were included.

The owner supplied this carton example as NonBoxable. It does not fit through a letterbox and is described here as Profile B (Non-Boxable parcel). Its reported fully packed dimensions total 475 mm, its longest side is 213 mm and its reported shipment weight is 500 g. These measurements fall within the supplied fully packed envelope of ≤900 mm combined dimensions, ≤600 mm longest side and ≤2,000 g. They do not guarantee carrier acceptance.

The recorded shipping selection was FedEx Next Day Delivery, fully tracked, to Spain. Vareya reports packing and label preparation in under 30 seconds for this example. That is an example-level preparation time, not an average, a service-level guarantee or evidence of the actual delivery time.

sections.heading: Germany: one-pouch mailer order (labelled Boxable)
paragraphs: Order #503062 contained one ORMUX Pineapple, listed as 120 g / 40 servings (FPF-0015-120). The reported branded bubble mailer measured 15 × 21 × 2 cm, with a shipment weight of 150 g. Protective material and a thank-you card were included.
The packed dimensions sit within the 28 × 26.5 × 3.2 cm letterbox envelope stated in the evidence sheet. Final service eligibility also depends on the destination and carrier requirements.

The shipping selection is recorded as a fully tracked PostNL letterbox service. Vareya reports packing and label preparation in under 15 seconds for this example. The sheet describes next-day delivery, but no delivery scan is included; actual arrival time is not established here.

sections.heading: The shared handling process
paragraphs: For both examples, Vareya describes bulk storage and picking bins, barcode scanning, expiry handling, and batch and lot registration. Products are packed with protection and a thank-you card. A return process applies when a return occurs.

Together, the examples illustrate how one supplement range can need more than one packaging format. A thin single-item order can be assessed for letterbox shipping; a multi-item order can require a compact carton. The appropriate choice starts with the packed order, not simply the product category.

sections.heading: What the photographs show
paragraphs: The product photographs are grouped with the corresponding order example. The bottle photographs show the three named products. The supplied carton image is a packaging illustration; its shipping label is fully masked, and the photograph is not proof of the recorded Spanish shipment.

The two ORMUX photographs show Lime, 60 g / 20 sachets; the German order record describes Pineapple, 120 g / 40 servings. They are product-format illustrations, not photographs of that exact order. The supplied marketing collages are not independent operational order evidence.

sections.heading: Source and scope
paragraphs: Source: Vareya’s PRIMAL FX Supplements Evidence Sheet and accompanying product photographs, supplied on 10 November 2026. These are two operational examples, not a controlled performance study. They do not establish a savings percentage, average processing speed or guaranteed cross-border delivery time.
